blogs.title: Meet BOFT: How Butterfly Factorization Makes Finetuning Large Models Cheap and Stable
blogs.description: A gentle introduction to Orthogonal Butterfly Finetuning (BOFT) for ML practitioners. Explain the motivation behind orthogonal finetuning, the problem with naive OFT parameter costs, and how butterfly factorization compresses dense orthogonal transforms to O(d log d) parameters. Use analogies (FFT/butterfly network) and show high-level results and when BOFT is a good choice vs LoRA or full finetuning.

blogs.title: From FFT to Finetuning: Visualizing the Butterfly Structure and Why It Works
blogs.description: A visual walkthrough of the butterfly graph and factorization. Step through small examples (d=8,16) to show how sparse factors compose into dense transforms, illustrate the information-transmission view from the paper, and include interactive diagrams or code snippets that let students see how paths connect inputs to outputs and how parameter count scales.

blogs.title: BOFT in Practice: Step-by-Step Guide to Adding Orthogonal Butterfly Finetuning to Your Model
blogs.description: A practical how-to for engineers: implementation tips, pseudocode for Cayley parameterization of 2x2 blocks, identity initialization, multiplicative dropout, choice of block-size m and b, batching considerations, and performance trade-offs. Include debugging tips (checking orthogonality, numerical stability), profiling advice, and simple recipes for Hugging Face Transformers and PyTorch.

blogs.title: BOFT vs LoRA vs OFT: Which Parameter-Efficient Finetuning Method Should You Use?
blogs.description: A comparative guide targeted at ML practitioners making design choices. Explain differences in update types (multiplicative orthogonal vs additive low-rank), parameter budgets, expressivity, spectral properties, training stability, and downstream performance. Provide decision rules and example configurations for vision transformers, LLMs, and diffusion models.

blogs.title: Beyond Block-Diagonal: Why Structured Sparsity (Butterfly) Generalizes Better Than Naive Sparsity
blogs.description: A conceptual post for students and researchers exploring inductive bias: contrast block-diagonal sparsity with butterfly sparsity, discuss why butterfly can approximate classic transforms (FFT, Hadamard) and how its structure helps generalization and prevents overfitting. Summarize the paper's theoretical intuitions and include simple experiments showing approximation vs parameter count.

blogs.title: Understanding Cayley Parameterization and Orthogonality Constraints for Stable Finetuning
blogs.description: A focused explainer on Cayley transform, skew-symmetric parameterization, and why preserving orthogonality matters for spectral norms and training stability. Cover numeric considerations, how identity initialization is achieved, and how orthogonality preservation compares to other regularization techniques in practice.

blogs.title: Tuning BOFT: Hyperparameters, Multiplicative Dropout and Practical Tricks for Robust Adaptation
blogs.description: A tactical guide to hyperparameter choices for BOFT: how many butterfly stages (m), block size (b), multiplicative dropout rates (p1, p2), initialization strategies, and stopping criteria. Share lessons from the paper's ablations and propose default settings for common model sizes and datasets to help practitioners get started quickly.

blogs.title: Case Studies: BOFT on Vision Transformers, LLMs and Diffusion Models — What Changed and Why
blogs.description: A narrative-driven post that summarizes the empirical applications from the paper. Walk through specific results, show performance gains relative to baselines, and explain which aspects of each modality (vision, language, generation) benefit from orthogonal transforms. Highlight real-world implications for researchers and teams considering PEFT at scale.

blogs.title: When Butterflies Aren't Enough: Limitations, Open Problems and Future Directions for BOFT
blogs.description: A balanced post for tech enthusiasts and researchers outlining BOFT's limitations (training runtime overhead, power-of-two constraints, unknown optimal topologies), open research questions (network topologies beyond butterfly, hybrid low-rank+sparse factorizations, faster GPU kernels), and promising directions for follow-up work.

blogs.title: Build a Toy: Implementing a 1-Layer BOFT Adapter from Scratch (Code Walkthrough)
blogs.description: A hands-on tutorial for students with code. Implement a minimal BOFT module that wraps a pretrained linear layer, using block 2x2 Cayley rotations to form butterfly components, demonstrate identity init and multiplicative dropout, and run a tiny finetuning experiment (e.g., few-shot classification) to show it works end-to-end.
